# HERMES station REST API reference

<!-- GENERATED by api/spec/gen_reference.py from api/spec/api-rest.yaml. Do not edit by hand. -->

The REST API of a HERMES station, served by hermes-radio-daemon under `/api/v2`. This page lists **every operation of the contract** (100); **30 are implemented in this build**, the rest are *planned* (in the spec, no handler yet, so they answer 404).

- New to the API? Start with the how-to guide: **[API-USAGE.md](API-USAGE.md)** (log in, log out, users, GPS, ...).
- Real-time (WebSocket) API: [API-WS-REFERENCE.md](API-WS-REFERENCE.md).
- The contract itself: [`api/spec/api-rest.yaml`](../api/spec/api-rest.yaml), version `2.0.0-draft.1`.

## Conventions

- **Base URL:** `http(s)://<station>/api/v2` (in this document, paths are relative to it).
- **Format:** JSON in and out, `snake_case`, integer Hz, ISO 8601 UTC timestamps. Writes send
  `Content-Type: application/json`; unknown fields are refused (422).
- **Authentication:** an opaque session token, from `POST /session`, sent as the `hermes_session`
  cookie (browsers) or `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (tools). No session: 401.
- **Roles**, lowest to highest: `readonly` < `user` < `operator` < `admin`. An operation's *Role* is
  the lowest role that may call it; a lower one gets 403.
- **CSRF:** a request that changes something (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`) authenticated with the
  *cookie* must carry an `Origin` naming the station, or `X-Hermes-CSRF: 1` (403 `csrf` otherwise).
  Bearer requests are exempt.
- **Collections** return `{"data": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}` and take `limit` (default 50, max 200)
  and `cursor`; `next_cursor` is absent on the last page.
- **Create** returns 201 with the object, **update** is `PATCH` with only the fields that change,
  **delete** returns 204. No `GET` changes anything.
- **Every response** has an `X-Request-Id` (send your own, up to 64 characters, and it is echoed).
- **Errors** are `application/problem+json` ([RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457)) with a
  stable string `code`, a `detail`, the `request_id`, and for validation failures `errors` per field.

### Standard errors

| Status | Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | Unauthorized | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). |
| 403 | Forbidden | The role is too low (`code` = `forbidden`). |
| 404 | NotFound | No such resource (`code` = `not_found`). |
| 409 | Conflict | Conflicts with the current state (`code` says which). |
| 413 | TooLarge | Over the size limit for HF (`code` = `too_large`). |
| 422 | Invalid | Validation failed (`code` = `invalid`; `errors` per field). |
| 429 | TooManyRequests | Too many failed logins (`code` = `rate_limited`). |
|  | NotRunning | Mercury is not running, so there is no modem to ask (`code` = `not_running`). |

<a id="op-factoryreset"></a>
### `POST /system/factory-reset`

**Erase the station's data, in two calls.** (`factoryReset`)

- Role: **admin**
- Status: **planned (not implemented yet)**

The first call (no body) returns a confirmation code valid for 60 seconds. The
second call, with that code, erases messages, attachments, users other than `root`
and settings, then reboots. It never deletes system directories.

**Request body** (`application/json`): object

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `confirmation_code` | string |  |  |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | First call — the code to confirm with. | `application/json` object |
| 202 | Second call — erasing, then rebooting. |  |
| 422 | Wrong or expired code (`code` = `bad_confirmation`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

<a id="op-runsetup"></a>
### `POST /setup`

**First-boot setup, once.** (`runSetup`)

- Role: **none (public)**
- Status: **implemented**

Accepted only until setup is completed, while no user but the installer's `root`
exists, and only with the one-time `setup_code` that the installer shows on the
console and writes to `/etc/hermes/setup-code`. Five wrong codes lock setup for 10
minutes. Creates the first admin, names the station and sets its language, time
zone, first radio profile and enabled apps. The UUCP name and mail domain are set
by the installer and are not changed here.

**Request body** (`application/json`, required): [SetupRequest](#schema-setuprequest)

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `setup_code` | string | yes | From the installer (console or `/etc/hermes/setup-code`); single use; write-only |
| `station_name` | string | yes | max length 64 |
| `callsign` | string or null |  | max length 16 |
| `country` | string or null |  | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; pattern `^[A-Z]{2}$` |
| `language` | [Locale](#schema-locale) | yes |  |
| `timezone` | string | yes |  |
| `admin` | object | yes |  |
| `radio_profile` | object |  |  |
| `apps` | array of string |  | Apps to enable (ids from `GET /apps`) |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 201 | Done; the new admin is logged in. | `application/json` [Session](#schema-session) |
| 403 | Wrong setup code (`code` = `bad_setup_code`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | Setup was already done (`code` = `setup_done`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | Validation failed (`code` = `invalid`; `errors` per field). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/setup" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "setup_code": "123456",
  "station_name": "Station Alpha",
  "language": "en",
  "timezone": "America/Sao_Paulo",
  "admin": {
    "username": "alice",
    "password": "a-long-passphrase"
  }
}'
```

<a id="op-login"></a>
### `POST /session`

**Log in.** (`login`)

- Role: **none (public)**
- Status: **implemented**

Sets the `hermes_session` cookie and also returns the token, for tools that use
`Authorization: Bearer`. Failed logins are limited to 5 a minute per address.

**Request body** (`application/json`, required): [LoginRequest](#schema-loginrequest)

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `username` | string | yes |  |
| `password` | string | yes | write-only |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 201 | Logged in. | `application/json` [Session](#schema-session) |
| 401 | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Too many failed logins (`code` = `rate_limited`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/session" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "username": "alice",
  "password": "a-long-passphrase"
}'
```

<a id="op-createuser"></a>
### `POST /users`

**Create a user and their mailbox.** (`createUser`)

- Role: **admin**
- Status: **implemented**

Also creates the Postfix/Dovecot mailbox through the station's `email_create_user` helper.

> **In this build:** The mailbox is not created yet: the station's `email_create_user` helper is not wired in. Only the account is created.

**Request body** (`application/json`, required): [UserCreate](#schema-usercreate)

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |

| `display_name` | string or null |  | Human name, optional; when null the UI shows the username; max length 64 |
| `role` | [Role](#schema-role) |  |  |
| `locale` | [Locale](#schema-locale) |  |  |
| `phone` | string |  |  |
| `location` | string |  |  |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 201 | Created. | `application/json` [User](#schema-user) |
| 403 | The role is too low (`code` = `forbidden`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | Conflicts with the current state (`code` says which). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | Validation failed (`code` = `invalid`; `errors` per field). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Example**

```bash

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
```

<a id="tag-messages"></a>
## messages

HERMES messages exchanged with other stations over UUCP, broadcast to every station listening, or exchanged with any LXMF address over Reticulum. **LXMF.** A message with `lxmf` instead of `recipients` goes from the sender's own LXMF address (or the station's) to one or more LXMF addresses: Sideband, NomadNet or MeshChat users, or users of other stations. Each recipient has its own LXMF delivery state, and `delivered` is a real receipt from the recipient. **Broadcast.** A message with `broadcast` instead of `recipients` goes to an area (`GET /areas`) on Mercury's broadcast plane, as a RaptorQ fountain carousel in Mercury's broadcast wire format (mercury `docs/BROADCAST-WIRE-FORMAT.md`). radiod's messaging layer runs the carousel in-process with Mercury's own carousel code. Any station listening in the same mode decodes it, even one that tunes in halfway through, and nobody acknowledges it. There is no negotiation on the broadcast plane: a broadcast goes out in the station's listen mode (`modem.config.listen_mode`), and only stations listening in that mode hear it. With `broadcast.encrypt`, the message is encrypted to the area as an NNCP area packet; otherwise it goes out in the clear, signed. Either way a receiver keeps one copy per broadcast, however many passes or paths bring it, and an encrypted one that a station missed can still reach it later through NNCP relaying over ARQ. The wire format is in `docs/api-design/broadcast.md`.

| [`getMessage`](#op-getmessage) | `GET /messages/{message_id}` | readonly | planned |
| [`updateDraft`](#op-updatedraft) | `PATCH /messages/{message_id}` | user | planned |

| [`decryptMessage`](#op-decryptmessage) | `POST /messages/{message_id}/decrypt` | user | planned |
| [`markRead`](#op-markread) | `PUT /messages/{message_id}/read` | readonly | planned |
| [`markUnread`](#op-markunread) | `DELETE /messages/{message_id}/read` | readonly | planned |

<a id="op-sendmessage"></a>
### `POST /messages/{message_id}/send`

**Queue a draft to each recipient (one UUCP job per recipient), or for broadcast.** (`sendMessage`)

- Role: **user**
- Status: **planned (not implemented yet)**

Safe to retry; recipients already queued are left as they are, and a broadcast
already queued or on the air is left as it is.

An LXMF message is handed to the LXMF router, one LXMF message per recipient; each
recipient's `state` follows it, up to `delivered`. A recipient reached only
through a backhaul link waits in the propagation node until that link is up.

A broadcast goes out in the station's listen mode (`modem.config.listen_mode`),
recorded as `broadcast.mode`, for `broadcast.cycles` passes of the
carousel; follow it on the `messages` topic, and the modem's side on
`modem.status.broadcast`. ARQ comes first: a broadcast waits (`waiting_arq`) while
an ARQ session holds the modem, and an ARQ session that starts while it is on the
air stops it (`preempted`). It goes on the air again once the link is idle; whether
it resumes or starts its carousel over is up to Mercury (open).

A broadcast is refused while the listen mode can't carry broadcast messages
(DATAC15, MFSK, MFSK500; 409 `code` = `listen_mode_unsuitable`).

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message_id` | path | integer (int64) | yes |  |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Queued; `recipients` carries each one's state and job id, or `broadcast` its state. | `application/json` [Message](#schema-message) |
| 429 | The user has sent `settings.tx_rate_limit.broadcasts_per_hour` broadcasts this hour (`code` = `rate_limited`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | Conflicts with the current state (`code` says which). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 413 | Over the size limit for HF (`code` = `too_large`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 507 | The UUCP spool for a recipient is full (`code` = `spool_full`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

<a id="op-stopbroadcast"></a>
### `POST /messages/{message_id}/stop`

**Stop a broadcast at the next frame boundary.** (`stopBroadcast`)

- Role: **user**
- Status: **planned (not implemented yet)**

`broadcast.state` becomes `stopped`. radiod stops handing frames to Mercury;
frames Mercury has already queued still go out. A broadcast still waiting for the
modem is taken out of the line. With `withdraw`, the station also sends a short cancel
object to the area: receivers drop a partial decode, and mark a copy they already
decoded as withdrawn (`broadcast.withdrawn_at`).

Its author may stop or withdraw it; anyone else needs `operator` (403 `forbidden`).

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message_id` | path | integer (int64) | yes |  |

**Request body** (`application/json`): object

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `withdraw` | boolean |  | default `False` |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Stopped. | `application/json` [Message](#schema-message) |
| 404 | No such resource (`code` = `not_found`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 409 | Not a broadcast, or not waiting or on the air (`code` = `not_broadcasting`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Change alias, frequency, mode or enabled. The UUCP configuration itself is never written.** (`updateStation`)

- Status: **planned (not implemented yet)**

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `uucp_name` | path | [UucpName](#schema-uucpname) | yes |  |

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alias` | string or null |  | pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$` |
| `display_name` | string or null |  | max length 64 |
| `frequency_hz` | integer or null |  | min 0 |
| `mode` | [Mode](#schema-mode) or null |  |  |
| `enabled` | boolean |  |  |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Updated. | `application/json` [Station](#schema-station) |
| 422 | Validation failed (`code` = `invalid`; `errors` per field). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

<a id="tag-reticulum"></a>
## reticulum

The station's Reticulum node: a transport and LXMF propagation node for phones on its Wi-Fi, with backhaul links to other stations over Mercury ARQ. LXMF messages themselves are messages (`channel` = `lxmf`). See `docs/api-design/reticulum.md`.

| Operation | Method and path | Role | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`getReticulum`](#op-getreticulum) | `GET /reticulum` | readonly | planned |
| [`getReticulumSettings`](#op-getreticulumsettings) | `GET /reticulum/settings` | operator | planned |
| [`updateReticulumSettings`](#op-updatereticulumsettings) | `PATCH /reticulum/settings` | admin | planned |
| [`listReticulumLinks`](#op-listreticulumlinks) | `GET /reticulum/links` | readonly | planned |
| [`getReticulumLink`](#op-getreticulumlink) | `GET /reticulum/links/{uucp_name}` | readonly | planned |
| [`putReticulumLink`](#op-putreticulumlink) | `PUT /reticulum/links/{uucp_name}` | admin | planned |
| [`deleteReticulumLink`](#op-deletereticulumlink) | `DELETE /reticulum/links/{uucp_name}` | admin | planned |
| [`listLxmfPeers`](#op-listlxmfpeers) | `GET /reticulum/peers` | readonly | planned |
| [`announceLxmf`](#op-announcelxmf) | `POST /reticulum/announce` | user | planned |

<a id="op-updatereticulumsettings"></a>
### `PATCH /reticulum/settings`

**Change the Reticulum node's settings.** (`updateReticulumSettings`)

- Role: **admin**
- Status: **planned (not implemented yet)**

**Request body** (`application/json`, required): [ReticulumSettings](#schema-reticulumsettings)

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | default `False` |
| `propagation` | object |  |  |
| `local` | object |  | How phones and computers on the station's Wi-Fi reach its node |
| `announce_interval_s` | integer |  | How often the station and its users' addresses are announced. Over backhaul, Reticulum's own announce cap applies; min 300; default `1800` |

| Status | Meaning | Body |

| 422 | Validation failed (`code` = `invalid`; `errors` per field). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

<a id="op-announcelxmf"></a>
### `POST /reticulum/announce`

**Announce your LXMF address now (or the station's).** (`announceLxmf`)

- Role: **user**
- Status: **planned (not implemented yet)**

The announce goes out on the Wi-Fi at once and over each backhaul link the next
time it is up; it never starts a call. Announcing for the station needs `operator`.

**Request body** (`application/json`): object

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as_station` | boolean |  | default `False` |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 202 | Announced. |  |
| 409 | Reticulum is off (`code` = `reticulum_off`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 429 | Announced too recently (`code` = `rate_limited`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Station-wide radio settings (default profile and fallback, tuning step, SWR limit, BFO).** (`getRadioSettings`)

- Role: **readonly**
- Status: **implemented**

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Settings. | `application/json` [RadioSettings](#schema-radiosettings) |
| 401 | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$BASE/radio/settings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

<a id="op-updateradiosettings"></a>
### `PATCH /radio/settings`

**Change station-wide radio settings.** (`updateRadioSettings`)

- Role: **admin**
- Status: **implemented**

**Request body** (`application/json`, required): [RadioSettingsPatch](#schema-radiosettingspatch)

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default_profile` | integer |  | min 0 |
| `default_profile_fallback_s` | integer or null |  | min 1 |
| `step_hz` | integer |  | min 1 |
| `swr_limit` | number |  | min 1.0 |
| `bfo_hz` | integer |  | sBitx only; refused (422) on Hamlib radios; min 0 |
| `tx_timeout_s` | integer |  | Refused (422) while the radio has no transmit timeout (`tx_timeout_s` null); min 10 |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Updated. | `application/json` [RadioSettings](#schema-radiosettings) |
| 422 | Validation failed (`code` = `invalid`; `errors` per field). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 401 | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 403 | The role is too low (`code` = `forbidden`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X PATCH "$BASE/radio/settings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "default_profile": 0
}'
```

<a id="tag-digi"></a>
## digi

Digital-mode traffic (FT8, CW, RTTY, D-STAR) sent and heard by the radio.

| Operation | Method and path | Role | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`getDigiLog`](#op-getdigilog) | `GET /digi/log` | readonly | implemented |
| [`getDigiSettings`](#op-getdigisettings) | `GET /radio/digi` | readonly | implemented |
| [`updateDigiSettings`](#op-updatedigisettings) | `PATCH /radio/digi` | operator | implemented |

<a id="op-getdigilog"></a>
### `GET /digi/log`

**Digital-mode traffic, newest first.** (`getDigiLog`)

- Role: **readonly**
- Status: **implemented**

Everything the radio decoded or sent in FT8, CW, RTTY, and every D-STAR header it
heard. The live feed is the `digi` WebSocket topic. Text and callsigns came over the
air: untrusted, render as plain text.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | query | [DigiMode](#schema-digimode) |  |  |
| `dir` | query | one of `rx`, `tx` |  |  |
| `callsign` | query | string |  | Entries from or to this callsign.; max length 16 |
| `since` | query | string (date-time) |  |  |
| `until` | query | string (date-time) |  |  |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | min 1; max 200; default `50` |
| `cursor` | query | string |  | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Entries. | `application/json` object |
| 401 | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$BASE/digi/log" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

<a id="op-getdigisettings"></a>
### `GET /radio/digi`

**CW, RTTY and D-STAR settings.** (`getDigiSettings`)

- Role: **readonly**
- Status: **implemented**

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Settings. | `application/json` [DigiSettings](#schema-digisettings) |
| 401 | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$BASE/radio/digi" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

<a id="op-updatedigisettings"></a>
### `PATCH /radio/digi`

**Change CW, RTTY, D-STAR or RADE V2 settings, voice encryption included.** (`updateDigiSettings`)

- Role: **operator**
- Status: **implemented**

**Request body** (`application/json`, required): [DigiSettings](#schema-digisettings)

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cw` | object |  |  |
| `rtty` | object |  |  |
| `dstar` | object |  |  |
| `rade` | object |  |  |
| `voice_codec` | one of `RADEV2`, `DSTAR` |  | The codec digital voice uses (radiod's `digital_voice_codec`). `DSTAR` needs the sBitx backend; refused while transmitting |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Applied. | `application/json` [DigiSettings](#schema-digisettings) |
| 422 | Validation failed (`code` = `invalid`; `errors` per field). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X PATCH "$BASE/radio/digi" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "cw": {
    "wpm": 5
  }
}'
```

## modem

Mercury, the HF modem.

| Operation | Method and path | Role | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

<a id="op-getmodemstatus"></a>
### `GET /modem`

**Mercury's link state (the same data as the `modem.status` topic).** (`getModemStatus`)

- Role: **readonly**
- Status: **implemented**

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Status. | `application/json` [ModemStatus](#schema-modemstatus) |
| 401 | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | Mercury is not running, so there is no modem to ask (`code` = `not_running`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$BASE/modem" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

<a id="op-getmodemconfig"></a>
### `GET /modem/config`

**The modem configuration.** (`getModemConfig`)

- Role: **operator**
- Status: **implemented**

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Configuration. | `application/json` [ModemConfig](#schema-modemconfig) |
| 401 | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | Mercury is not running, so there is no modem to ask (`code` = `not_running`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$BASE/modem/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

<a id="op-updatemodemconfig"></a>
### `PATCH /modem/config`

**Change the modem configuration. Applied before the reply; a change that fails is not saved.** (`updateModemConfig`)

- Role: **admin**
- Status: **implemented**

**Request body** (`application/json`, required): [ModemConfigPatch](#schema-modemconfigpatch)

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tx_gain_db` | number |  | min -20; max 20 |
| `waterfall` | boolean |  |  |
| `listen_mode` | [BroadcastMode](#schema-broadcastmode) |  | The mode the station listens in while no ARQ link is up, and sends its broadcasts in: one setting for receive and transmit. Mercury's broadcast chat (`modem.chat`, plane `broadcast`) uses it too. Default DATAC3 |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Applied and saved. | `application/json` [ModemConfig](#schema-modemconfig) |
| 409 | `listen_mode` changed while an ARQ link is up or a broadcast is on the air (`code` = `busy`); `modem.status` says which (`link`, `broadcast.state`). Or changed to a mode that can't carry broadcast messages while some are waiting (`code` = `broadcasts_waiting`). Nothing was applied. | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 422 | Not applied (a validation error). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 503 | Mercury is not running, so there is no modem to ask (`code` = `not_running`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X PATCH "$BASE/modem/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "tx_gain_db": 0
}'
```

<a id="op-liststationpositions"></a>
### `GET /gps/stations`

**Every known station with its last-known position, for the map.** (`listStationPositions`)

- Role: **readonly**
- Status: **planned (not implemented yet)**

Stations this one can reach (from `/etc/uucp/sys`), each with the position it last
reported over the air or was given manually. Stations with no known position are
still listed, with null position fields. A reported position is a claim, not an
identity.

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Stations with their last-known positions. | `application/json` object |
| 401 | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

<a id="op-getcurrenttrip"></a>
### `GET /gps/trip`

**The current trip and its recorded positions (the breadcrumb).** (`getCurrentTrip`)

- Role: **readonly**
- Status: **planned (not implemented yet)**

The station's open trip: every position fix is stored in the database and listed
here, oldest first, so the map can draw the breadcrumb. A trip opens automatically
and closes only via `POST /gps/trip/close`, so one is always open; `ended_at` is
null until then.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | min 1; max 200; default `50` |
| `cursor` | query | string |  | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | The current trip and its points. | `application/json` object |
| 401 | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

<a id="op-closetrip"></a>
### `POST /gps/trip/close`

**Close the current trip and start a new one.** (`closeTrip`)

- Role: **operator**
- Status: **planned (not implemented yet)**

Sets `ended_at` on the open trip and starts a new one; the next position fix is
recorded in the new trip. Nothing is deleted, so closed trips stay in the history.
Returns the trip that was closed.

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | The trip that was closed. | `application/json` [Trip](#schema-trip) |
| 409 | No trip is open (`code` = `no_open_trip`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |
| 401 | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

- Status: **planned (not implemented yet)**

Each app (chat, GPS, radio, mail…) is an independent web app served under its own
path and built only on this API. The station's shell reads this list to show the apps
a user may open. Apps are installed and updated as Debian packages, not through the API.

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Apps. | `application/json` object |
| 401 | Not logged in, or the session ended (`code` = `unauthenticated`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

<a id="op-updateapp"></a>
### `PATCH /apps/{app_id}`

**Enable or disable an app, or change who may open it.** (`updateApp`)

- Role: **admin**
- Status: **planned (not implemented yet)**

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_id` | path | string | yes | pattern `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$` |

**Request body** (`application/json`, required): object

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean |  |  |
| `min_role` | [Role](#schema-role) |  |  |

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Updated. | `application/json` [App](#schema-app) |
| 404 | No such resource (`code` = `not_found`). | `application/problem+json` [Problem](#schema-problem) |

| `cycle` | integer or null |  | Outgoing only; the pass of the carousel on the air, from 1; min 1 |
| `frames_sent` | integer |  | Outgoing only |
| `frames_total` | integer |  | Outgoing only; every pass of the carousel |

<a id="schema-broadcastcreate"></a>
### BroadcastCreate

The whole broadcast (the `.hmp` file with its attachment, plus the header) is at
most 1.44 MB; larger is refused at send (413).

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `area` | [AreaName](#schema-areaname) | yes | A broadcast area's name, as in the NNCP configuration; pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$` |
| `cycles` | integer |  | Passes of the carousel. A receiver that falls short decodes nothing at all, and extra passes cost airtime but not delivery time, so err high on a fading path; min 1; max 16; default `2` |
| `with_author` | boolean |  | Put the sender's username on the air, so receivers can show it and reply to the user. Without it the broadcast comes from the station; the audit log records the user either way; default `False` |
| `encrypt` | boolean |  | Encrypt to the area as an NNCP area packet. Needs the area's keys (`has_keys`); otherwise the message goes out in the clear, signed; default `False` |
| `expires_at` | [Timestamp](#schema-timestamp) or null |  | Receivers drop the broadcast after this, decoded or not |
| `supersedes` | integer or null (int64) |  | An earlier broadcast of this station to the same area that this one replaces |

<a id="schema-broadcastfilemode"></a>
### BroadcastFileMode

The listen modes that can carry a broadcast message: the carousel's symbols are
41 bytes, so a frame needs at least that much room.

Type: one of `DATAC1`, `DATAC3`, `DATAC4`, `DATAC17`, `QAM16C2`

<a id="schema-broadcastmode"></a>
### BroadcastMode

A Mercury payload mode the station can listen in (`mercury -m`, the `MODE`
command): the modes Mercury can switch to at runtime. Sender and receivers must use
the same one. Measured by Mercury (`docs/MODES.md`, `docs/BROADCAST-FILE.md`):

| mode | index | frame | bit/s | bandwidth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DATAC1 | 0 | 510 B | 976 | 1687 Hz |
| DATAC3 | 1 | 126 B | 316 | 562 Hz |
| DATAC4 | 3 | 54 B | 84 | 250 Hz |
| DATAC15 | 7 | 30 B | 64 | 187 Hz |
| DATAC17 | 9 | 1180 B | 1407 | 2062 Hz |
| QAM16C2 | 10 | 1213 B | 3130 | 2062 Hz |
| MFSK | 11 | 98 B | 61 | 1000 Hz |
| MFSK500 | 12 | 98 B | 31 | 500 Hz |

Broadcast chat (`modem.chat`, plane `broadcast`) works in any of them; a broadcast
message needs a `BroadcastFileMode`. DATAC0, DATAC13, DATAC14, DATAC16 and FSK_LDPC
can't be selected at runtime. A weak but steady path needs a more robust mode, while
a fading one needs more `cycles`.

Type: one of `DATAC1`, `DATAC3`, `DATAC4`, `DATAC15`, `DATAC17`, `QAM16C2`, `MFSK`, `MFSK500`

| `waterfall` | boolean |  |  |

<a id="schema-radiosettings"></a>
### RadioSettings

Settings radiod keeps once for the station, not per profile.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default_profile` | integer | yes | min 0 |
| `default_profile_fallback_s` | integer or null | yes | How long another profile stays active before the radio returns to `default_profile`; null never returns. radiod's `main:default_profile_fallback_timeout` (-1 there for null); min 1 |
| `step_hz` | integer | yes | The tuning step; min 1 |
| `swr_limit` | number | yes | The SWR above which high-SWR protection trips, e.g. 2.5 for 2.5:1. radiod stores it as SWR × 10 (`main:reflected_threshold` = 25); min 1.0 |
| `bfo_hz` | integer or null | yes | The sBitx's beat-frequency oscillator, an absolute frequency in Hz (`main:bfo`, e.g. 40035000). null on Hamlib radios, which don't use it; min 0 |
| `tx_timeout_s` | integer or null |  | The longest single transmission; after it the station unkeys and reports `tx_timeout`. null when the radio backend doesn't support one yet; min 10 |

<a id="schema-radiosettingspatch"></a>
### RadioSettingsPatch

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default_profile` | integer |  | min 0 |
| `default_profile_fallback_s` | integer or null |  | min 1 |
| `step_hz` | integer |  | min 1 |
| `swr_limit` | number |  | min 1.0 |
| `bfo_hz` | integer |  | sBitx only; refused (422) on Hamlib radios; min 0 |
| `tx_timeout_s` | integer |  | Refused (422) while the radio has no transmit timeout (`tx_timeout_s` null); min 10 |
